change_history.description: Initial comprehensive analysis of camunda-bpmn-model issues focusing on BPMN model parsing and builder API

features.title: Asynchronous Multi-Instance Support

features.business_value: Fine-grained async control for multi-instance patterns

features.title: Timeout Task Listener

features.technical_scope: Add builder methods for timeout task listeners in user task workflows, support event definitions as child elements
features.business_value: Enable time-based task listener patterns for SLA enforcement

features.title: DataStoreReference Support

features.technical_scope: Add DataStoreReference element support to model and builder API

features.title: Data Store Support

features.technical_scope: Implement Data Store elements mirroring existing Data Object functionality
features.business_value: Support persistent data modeling in BPMN processes

features.title: Clone functionality for BpmnModelInstance
features.description: Enable creating independent copies of BPMN model instances
features.business_value: Support process template patterns and model manipulation scenarios

features.title: Performer Support

features.title: TextAnnotation and MultiInstanceLoopCharacteristics

features.business_value: Support process documentation and iterative activity patterns

features.title: DataObject Support

features.technical_scope: Implement data object elements in model and builder

enhancements.title: Java 8 Migration
enhancements.description: Modernize codebase to use Java 8 language features

enhancements.title: Builder Element Access
enhancements.description: Make builder's current element publicly accessible
technical_details: Expose current element for advanced use cases
Support scenarios not fully covered by standard builder patterns

enhancements.title: Convenience Methods for Class References
enhancements.description: Add convenience methods allowing class references instead of string-based class names

enhancements.title: Auto-casting for getModelElementById

Cleaner client code without explicit casting

documentation.title: OSGi Headers

architectural.title: Explicit Element Types
architectural.description: Refactor model to include explicit element type definitions
technical_details: Improve type safety in model API

key_insights.insight: BPMN 2.0 specification is extensive, and practical implementations add element support incrementally based on user needs. The repository shows systematic addition of data elements, human workflow elements, and loop characteristics over time.
action_items: Prioritize BPMN element coverage based on usage patterns and user needs
Design model architecture to easily add new element types
Maintain consistent API patterns across element implementations
Document which BPMN 2.0 elements are supported and roadmap for others

key_insights.insight: Fluent builder APIs evolve to support both common patterns (standard methods) and advanced scenarios (element access, custom extensions). Balance between convenience and flexibility is key.
action_items: Design builder API with escape hatches for advanced use cases
Provide both string-based and type-safe method variants
Make current builder state accessible when needed
Support method chaining and fluent patterns consistently

key_insights.insight: BPMN models need to support cloning, serialization, and deserialization for template patterns and model manipulation scenarios. Deep copy semantics must preserve all model state.
action_items: Implement robust clone/copy functionality for model instances
Use serialization/deserialization for deep copying
Ensure all model state is properly captured in serialization
Support model templates and dynamic model generation

key_insights.insight: Type safety improvements (generic type inference, class references instead of strings, explicit element types) reduce errors and improve developer experience. Early architecture decision to use explicit types enables validation.
action_items: Use generics for type-safe element retrieval
Prefer class references over string-based type names
Define explicit element type hierarchy in model
Enable compile-time checking where possible

key_insights.insight: Asynchronous execution control needs to be available at multiple granularity levels: whole activity body, individual elements within multi-instance, and event-based triggers. Coarse-grained async control is insufficient.
action_items: Design async execution model with multiple granularity levels
Support async at activity, element, and event levels
Allow fine-grained control for multi-instance patterns
Consider timeout and timer-based async patterns

key_insights.insight: BPMN data modeling (DataObject, DataStore, DataStoreReference) is often added later as users need to model information flows alongside control flows. These elements are lower priority than core execution elements.
action_items: Support data elements for complete BPMN coverage
Prioritize execution elements over data modeling elements initially
Maintain API consistency across data element types
Consider how data elements map to runtime variables

pain_points.description: BPMN 2.0 specification is large, and users need features incrementally based on their process patterns
pain_points.user_impact: Users must wait for specific BPMN elements to be implemented or work around missing elements

pain_points.description: Standard builder patterns don't cover all advanced use cases, requiring escape hatches
pain_points.user_impact: Advanced users need direct element access to accomplish tasks not supported by fluent API

pain_points.description: Library must balance using modern Java features with compatibility for user environments
pain_points.user_impact: Users on older Java versions cannot use newer library versions

architectural_decisions.rationale: Enable model validation and default value support through explicit type system
architectural_decisions.impact: Foundation for schema-based validation and type-safe API, set direction for entire model architecture

architectural_decisions.rationale: Provide intuitive, chainable API for BPMN model construction
architectural_decisions.impact: Consistent API experience across all BPMN elements, ongoing pattern for new element support

architectural_decisions.rationale: Leverage existing serialization/deserialization to implement deep copy
architectural_decisions.impact: Ensures clone completeness by reusing serialization logic, simpler implementation

architectural_decisions.rationale: Modernize codebase to use lambda expressions, streams, and improved type inference
architectural_decisions.impact: Better developer experience, improved code readability, but requires Java 8+ for users

architectural_decisions.decision: Generic Type Inference for Element Retrieval
architectural_decisions.rationale: Eliminate redundant type casts through generic method signatures
architectural_decisions.impact: Cleaner client code, better IDE support, maintained type safety

architectural_decisions.rationale: Add BPMN elements based on user demand rather than complete spec coverage upfront
architectural_decisions.impact: Faster initial delivery, focused development on used features, some user needs unmet until implementation

common_patterns.observation: BPMN elements added one by one as user needs emerge rather than implementing entire specification upfront
Builder API enhanced with convenience methods, escape hatches, and type-safe variants over time
Continuous improvement of type safety through generics, explicit types, and compile-time checking
Regular dependency updates for testing frameworks and build tooling

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Design UML metamodel with explicit element type definitions from the start. This enables validation, default values, and type-safe APIs.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Camunda's early decision to use explicit element types (Issue #1) was foundational for the entire model architecture. This enabled validation and type safety throughout the project.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Provide fluent builder APIs for model construction with consistent patterns. Include escape hatches for advanced scenarios not covered by standard methods.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Builder APIs provide excellent developer experience for common cases, but need extensibility points for advanced use cases.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Use generic methods for model element retrieval to eliminate redundant type casts and improve code clarity.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Generic type inference improves developer experience with cleaner code and better IDE support while maintaining type safety.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Prefer class references over string-based type names in APIs to enable compile-time checking and refactoring support.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: String-based type names are error-prone and don't support refactoring. Class references provide better IDE integration.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Implement model cloning using serialization/deserialization to ensure complete state copying and consistency with persistence logic.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Reusing serialization logic for cloning ensures completeness and reduces code duplication.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Implement UML metamodel elements incrementally based on user needs rather than complete specification coverage upfront. Document coverage gaps clearly.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Complete specification coverage delays delivery. Incremental approach focuses effort on used features.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Design async execution model with multiple granularity levels: whole activity, individual elements, and event-based triggers.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Coarse-grained async control is insufficient for complex patterns. Fine-grained control enables performance optimization.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Make current builder state accessible to support advanced use cases and custom extensions not covered by standard API.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Builders need escape hatches for scenarios not anticipated by standard patterns.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: If targeting OSGi environments, configure proper manifest headers in build configuration.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: OSGi deployment requires specific manifest metadata that should be generated automatically.

actionable_items_for_uml_codex.description: Balance using modern Java features (lambdas, streams) with compatibility requirements of target environments.
actionable_items_for_uml_codex.learning: Modern Java improves code quality but creates minimum version requirements for users.
